title: Cancers of unknown primary
bottleneck: In 3 to 5% of cancers, metastatic disease is found without an identifiable primary tumor despite extensive workup, leaving oncologists to treat empirically with broad chemotherapy regimens rather than site-specific targeted therapy.
why_it_blocks: Modern oncology is organized around the primary site and its molecular drivers; without knowing the origin, patients miss targeted and immunotherapy options tied to specific cancer types.
current_state: Gene-expression and methylation-based classifiers, plus tissue-of-origin prediction from circulating tumor DNA in multi-cancer blood tests, are improving primary-site identification. Empiric therapy remains standard for many such patients while these tools are validated. Accurate origin prediction matters because site-specific therapies and immunotherapy eligibility increasingly depend on tumor type. As molecular classifiers improve, treatment for these patients is gradually shifting from empiric chemotherapy toward guided therapy.
